MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
DevOps / Platform Engineering | CI/CD & Test Infrastructure
Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation and test-infrastructure engineer with experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines, ephemeral Kubernetes test environments, and automation tooling. Owns GitLab CI pipelines supporting three product teams and has reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes. Hands-on with Docker, Helm, Kubernetes at namespace level, and Terraform through personal infrastructure projects. Building further Kubernetes administration knowledge while transitioning toward DevOps and platform engineering.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
CI/CD and automation: GitLab CI, Jenkins, pipeline optimization, artifact publishing, automated test workflows
Containers and orchestration: Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes (namespace-level access; test environments), k3s (personal homelab)
Infrastructure and operations: Terraform (personal project), Ansible (basic), Linux, Git, PostgreSQL
Monitoring and observability: Grafana, Prometheus, Loki; test metrics dashboards
Programming and scripting: Python, Bash, Java (test code), SQL
Testing: pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman
Cloud learning: AWS EC2 and S3 basics (personal learning)

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software | Wroclaw | 2021–Present
- Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams (~25 developers), covering build, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages and artifact publishing.
- Reduced average pipeline duration from 38 to 14 minutes by profiling workflows, parallelizing test jobs, caching dependencies and separating end-to-end testing into its own stage; monthly CI runner costs fell by about 30%.
- Built short-lived merge-request test environments for applications, PostgreSQL and seeded data, deploying with Docker Compose and later Helm to the company’s shared Kubernetes cluster. Environments are automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
- Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of approximately 900 tests; reduced the flaky-test rate from 7% to below 1%.
- Built test-result collection and Grafana dashboards using Python, PostgreSQL and the GitLab API to help teams identify flaky-test patterns.
- Wrote Bash and Python tooling to seed PostgreSQL test data.
- Authored an internal guide to CI workflows used in team onboarding; mentored two QA interns in 2023.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House | Wroclaw | 2019–2021
- Tested web and mobile applications for client projects using manual and automated approaches.
- Introduced a Java and Selenium automated regression suite for the largest client project.
- Configured Jenkins jobs to run nightly regression tests.

Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
- Investigated customer issues using logs and databases and reproduced bugs for developers.

SELECTED INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS
Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal | 2024–2025
- Built a three-node Raspberry Pi 5 k3s cluster, deploying applications from a Git repository with Argo CD.
- Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, with Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS.
- Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS using Terraform; used Ansible at a basic level.

Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments | Odrava Health | 2023–2024
- Implemented per-merge-request environments for application testing and review, with seeded PostgreSQL data and end-to-end tests running against each environment.
- Automated environment deployment through GitLab CI and Helm, and automatic cleanup after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.

CI Pipeline Speed-up | Odrava Health | 2022
- Profiled CI pipelines across three teams, parallelized test jobs, introduced dependency caching and split end-to-end testing into a separate stage.
- Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly CI runner costs by about 30%.

EDUCATION
BEng, Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018

CERTIFICATIONS AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) preparation; exam booked for January 2027 (not yet certified)

LANGUAGES
Polish (native) | English (C1) | German (A2)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, clear, metrics-led CV with a logical structure and credible progression from QA automation into DevOps and platform engineering. The Professional Summary accurately frames the transition without overstating Kubernetes or cloud expertise. The strongest evidence includes ownership of GitLab CI for three product teams, pipeline reduction from 38 to 14 minutes, a 30% runner-cost reduction, ephemeral Kubernetes environments, and flaky-test reduction from 7% to below 1%. The selected projects reinforce the target direction and add useful operational detail. The main content limitation is that the document demonstrates strong CI/test infrastructure experience more clearly than broad cloud infrastructure engineering, systems design, networking, or security experience.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses conventional section headings, readable text formatting, standard date and job-title patterns, and relevant keywords such as GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Helm, Kubernetes, Terraform, AWS, Linux, Grafana, Prometheus, PostgreSQL, Python and Bash. It avoids tables, graphics, columns and unusual formatting that could impair parsing. Keyword coverage is good for CI/CD, containers, Kubernetes test environments and observability. ATS alignment would improve slightly if the CV used the exact supported terms 'infrastructure as code', 'TLS', 'certificate management', 'technical documentation', 'stakeholder collaboration' and 'system design' in context rather than relying mainly on tool names and project descriptions. It should not add Terragrunt, mTLS, production cloud ownership or unsupported security claims.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document is a credible partial match for the role, especially for hands-on infrastructure engineering around CI/CD, containerized environments, Kubernetes namespace-level operations, observability and automation. It also shows analytical thinking through measurable pipeline optimization and communication/technical leadership through ownership of shared pipelines, internal documentation and mentoring. AWS basics are truthfully included as personal learning. The candidate's material shows gaps against several central requirements: strong Terraform and Terragrunt, production-scale cloud environment design and operation, mTLS, broader networking, direct IoT or remote-device integration, and backend/full-stack experience. Kubernetes cluster administration and production on-call experience are also limited according to the candidate's notes, although they are not explicit requirements in the ad. These are candidate-experience gaps, not defects that can be solved by wording. The CV appropriately avoids claiming them.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, make the supported system-design and infrastructure-as-code evidence more explicit without overstating scope. For example, revise the final two sentences to: 'Designs and maintains CI/CD-driven test infrastructure, including short-lived Kubernetes environments, Helm deployments and automated cleanup. Hands-on Terraform and AWS exposure comes from personal infrastructure projects; Kubernetes production-cluster administration remains outside current scope.' This is more directly aligned with the role while preserving the current truthful qualification level.

2. In the Professional Experience section under 'QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure)', revise the ephemeral-environment bullet to include the supported infrastructure-as-code and TLS-related terminology only where accurate. For example: 'Built short-lived merge-request environments for applications, PostgreSQL and seeded data, using Docker Compose and Helm on a shared Kubernetes cluster; automated deployment and cleanup through GitLab CI.' Do not describe this as cluster infrastructure ownership or production cloud operations.

3. In the same Odrava Health section, strengthen the existing evidence of technical leadership and stakeholder communication by revising the documentation bullet to: 'Authored and maintained internal technical documentation for CI workflows, used in team onboarding, and mentored two QA interns in 2023.' This uses the candidate's documented experience and better addresses the requirement for clear communication and leading technical topics.

4. In the Technical Skills section, change 'Terraform (personal project)' to 'Infrastructure as code: Terraform (personal Hetzner VPS project)' and change 'AWS EC2 and S3 basics (personal learning)' to 'Cloud: AWS EC2 and S3 basics (personal learning); Hetzner VPS (personal project).' This makes the scope and context immediately clear to both recruiters and ATS systems.

5. In the Homelab project, retain 'cert-manager for TLS' and add the supported networking context by changing the relevant bullet to: 'Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, with Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS certificate management.' Do not add mTLS, SSL/TLS security architecture, network design or production-security claims because they are not supported by the candidate information.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, professional, readable, and substantially stronger than the original source material. It uses clear section headings, quantified achievements, relevant project examples, and honest qualification wording. The strongest evidence is the GitLab CI ownership, pipeline reduction from 38 to 14 minutes, 30% runner-cost reduction, ephemeral Kubernetes environments, and reduction in flaky tests from 7% to below 1%. The main content limitation is that the document presents strong QA/test-infrastructure experience but only limited direct evidence of cloud infrastructure architecture, stakeholder leadership, security, and production operations required by this role.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: ATS compatibility is strong: the CV uses conventional headings, plain text formatting, standard job titles, dates, employer names, and keyword-rich skills sections. Relevant terms such as Terraform, Kubernetes, Helm, GitLab CI, AWS, Linux, Grafana, Prometheus, TLS, Python, Java, and PostgreSQL are present. The document is likely to parse reliably and should perform well for CI/CD, test infrastructure, and junior-to-mid DevOps searches. It will be less competitive for this specific role because the ad's central terms Terragrunt, mTLS, cloud environment design, system architecture, certificate management, and infrastructure operations are either absent or only partially evidenced. Terragrunt and mTLS must not be added without genuine experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV shows credible hands-on infrastructure-adjacent engineering through ephemeral Kubernetes environments, Helm, Docker, CI/CD ownership, a k3s homelab, Terraform on Hetzner, observability tooling, and AWS EC2/S3 learning. It also demonstrates analytical thinking and communication through pipeline profiling, measurable optimization, internal documentation, onboarding support, and mentoring. The main gaps are strong Terraform and Terragrunt, production cloud infrastructure operations, mTLS, broader networking and security, IoT or remote-device integration, and backend/full-stack experience. Kubernetes experience is accurately scoped to namespace-level access rather than cluster administration. The profile is therefore a truthful but partial match, strongest for a junior or developing platform/infrastructure position rather than the full scope implied by this contractor role.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, clear, truthful CV for a QA-to-DevOps transition. It uses measurable outcomes effectively, including the reduction in pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes, approximately 30% lower runner costs, and the reduction in flaky tests from 7% to below 1%. The structure is easy to scan and the selected infrastructure projects strengthen the transition narrative. The main content limitation is that the CV presents relevant platform-adjacent experience but does not sufficiently distinguish production/shared-cluster responsibilities from personal or test-environment work. It also gives limited evidence of system design, security, networking, stakeholder leadership, and cloud operations at the level expected for this contractor role.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly: it uses conventional section headings, standard text formatting, clear job titles, dates, and keyword-rich skills. Relevant terms such as GitLab CI, Kubernetes, Helm, Terraform, Docker, Linux, AWS, Prometheus, Grafana, PostgreSQL, Python, and Java are present. AI screening is likely to recognize a credible junior-to-mid DevOps or platform-engineering profile, but the probability of passing this particular screening is reduced by the absence of Terragrunt, mutual TLS/mTLS, SSL/TLS as a networking/security competency, system architecture, and cloud-environment operations terminology. Do not add unsupported keywords merely to match the advertisement. The current CKA wording is appropriately transparent and must remain clearly marked as not yet certified.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with the role's infrastructure-engineering, CI/CD, Kubernetes-adjacent, observability, analytical-thinking, and technical-documentation aspects. It shows ownership of CI pipelines for three teams, stakeholder enablement through merge-request environments, and clear quantified problem-solving results. It partially aligns with hands-on cloud infrastructure through a personal Hetzner Terraform project and AWS EC2/S3 learning, but the candidate's material shows no substantial AWS production experience. Strong Terraform and Terragrunt is a gap: Terraform is limited to a personal project and Terragrunt is not present. Good systems architecture and system design are not strongly evidenced. Networking involving mTLS is a gap; the CV shows TLS certificate management through cert-manager but not mutual TLS or broader network design. Practical security awareness is only weakly evidenced. IoT, automotive, and remote-device integration are gaps. Backend/full-stack experience is limited, although Java test-code experience is shown. Linux is shown, but virtual-machine experience is not. The strongest alignment is with a junior or developing platform/DevOps scope rather than independently shaping production fleet-connectivity architecture from the start.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. In the Professional Summary, make the operating scope more precise while preserving the strong transition narrative. Change the wording about Kubernetes and infrastructure experience to explicitly distinguish shared-cluster namespace-level work, personal infrastructure projects, and test-environment operations. For example: "QA automation and test-infrastructure engineer with experience owning CI/CD for three product teams, designing ephemeral Kubernetes test environments, and building automation and observability tooling. Hands-on with Docker, Helm, Kubernetes at namespace level, and Terraform in a personal Hetzner project; currently developing broader Kubernetes administration and cloud-infrastructure capability." This prevents the document from implying cluster administration or production cloud ownership.

2. In the Technical Skills section, change "Infrastructure and operations" to "Infrastructure as Code and Operations" and keep the scope qualifiers directly beside the relevant tools: "Terraform (personal Hetzner project), Ansible (basic), Linux, Git, PostgreSQL." This improves matching for the advertisement's infrastructure-as-code language without overstating Terraform depth.

3. In the Technical Skills section, revise the monitoring line to make the supported observability experience more explicit: "Monitoring and observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki; Grafana dashboards for CI/test metrics; test-result collection via Python, PostgreSQL, and GitLab API." This better connects the existing tools to the role's requirement that services be observable and reliable.

4. In the Professional Experience section under Odrava Health Software, revise the first bullet to emphasize technical ownership and stakeholder scope without claiming formal infrastructure leadership. For example: "Owned GitLab CI pipeline design and maintenance for three product teams (~25 developers), covering build, unit, integration, and end-to-end testing stages and artifact publishing." Use "design and maintenance" only for the pipeline work already described; do not describe ownership of the Kubernetes cluster.

5. In the Odrava Health Software section, combine or revise the two ephemeral-environment bullets to describe the system design decisions more directly. For example: "Designed and implemented short-lived merge-request environments containing the application, PostgreSQL, seeded data, and automated end-to-end execution; deployed through GitLab CI and Helm to the shared Kubernetes cluster and automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity." This makes the existing architecture and lifecycle work easier for a recruiter to identify.

6. In the Odrava Health Software section, strengthen the stakeholder-leadership evidence by revising the review-environment bullet to: "Enabled QA and product stakeholders to review features before merge through per-merge-request application environments with seeded PostgreSQL data and automated end-to-end tests." The current wording is already accurate; this version puts stakeholder enablement earlier and uses the job advertisement's language more directly.

7. In the Selected Infrastructure Projects section, retain the Homelab project but make its scope and technologies more ATS-readable by changing the first two bullets to: "Built and operated a three-node Raspberry Pi 5 k3s cluster for personal learning, deploying applications from Git with Argo CD" and "Implemented personal observability and ingress components with Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Traefik, and cert-manager for TLS certificate management." This clearly shows hands-on operation while avoiding any implication that this was a production enterprise platform.

8. In the Certifications and Professional Development section, keep "Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) preparation; exam scheduled for January 2027 (not yet certified)" exactly in substance. Do not label CKA as an obtained certification, place it in a completed-certifications list, or shorten the wording in a way that could imply certification has already been earned.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear section headings, quantified achievements, relevant infrastructure projects, and unusually good transparency about Kubernetes access, personal Terraform work, and the uncompleted CKA. The strongest evidence is the CI/CD ownership, pipeline reduction from 38 to 14 minutes, 30% runner-cost reduction, ephemeral Kubernetes environments, observability dashboards, and stakeholder enablement. The main content limitation is that the CV presents a compelling transition toward DevOps/platform engineering but only partially demonstrates the broader cloud infrastructure, networking, systems architecture, and security scope of this particular contractor role. The selected projects section also repeats some content already covered under Odrava Health, which slightly reduces concision.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly: it uses standard headings, plain text formatting, conventional job titles, explicit technologies, measurable outcomes, and no parsing-risk tables, columns, graphics, or unusual symbols. It contains strong matching terms including CI/CD, GitLab CI, Jenkins, Terraform, Kubernetes, Helm, Docker, Linux, Prometheus, Grafana, PostgreSQL, AWS, infrastructure as code, observability, and TLS certificate management. AI screening probability is moderate to good for a junior-to-mid DevOps or platform-engineering profile, but lower for this specific role because the CV does not support or show Terragrunt, mTLS, production cloud operations, or broader systems architecture. Do not add those terms unless the candidate gains genuine experience with them.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with the role's infrastructure-engineering, automation, observability, analytical-thinking, communication, and technical-topic ownership requirements. It also provides relevant AWS exposure, Linux experience, and a JVM-adjacent background through Java test automation. The strongest role-relevant evidence is the design and operation of short-lived Kubernetes environments, Terraform provisioning of a Hetzner VPS, GitOps homelab operations, and collaboration with QA and product stakeholders. However, the candidate's material indicates gaps in strong Terraform/Terragrunt experience, formal systems architecture and system design, mTLS, production cloud operations, IoT or remote-device integration, backend development, and virtual machines. These are job-alignment gaps rather than document defects. The culture fit is reasonably suggested through ownership, technical documentation, mentoring, and enabling teams to collaborate, but the CV should remain evidence-based rather than adding unsupported claims about Corvale's values.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. In the Professional Summary, make the infrastructure-engineering scope more explicit without overstating cloud experience. For example, change the opening to: "QA automation and test-infrastructure engineer with hands-on infrastructure engineering experience across CI/CD, ephemeral Kubernetes environments, infrastructure as code, and observability tooling." Retain the existing qualification that Kubernetes access was at namespace level and that Terraform/cloud work includes a personal Hetzner project.

2. In the Technical Skills section, add the supported collaboration and technical-leadership terms already evidenced by the CV. Under CI/CD and automation or in a separate "Technical Leadership and Collaboration" line, add: "CI workflow documentation, stakeholder enablement, technical onboarding, mentoring." These are supported by the internal CI guide, QA/product review environments, and mentoring of two interns, and may improve matching for the requirement to lead technical topics and bring stakeholders along.

3. In the Odrava Health experience, revise the first and fourth bullets so the stakeholder and ownership impact is more direct. For example, change the fourth bullet to: "Enabled QA and product stakeholders to review features before merge through per-merge-request application environments with seeded PostgreSQL data and automated end-to-end tests." If space permits, append the supported outcome: "and documented the CI workflow used for team onboarding." This consolidates evidence that is currently split across separate bullets.

4. Reduce repetition between Professional Experience and Selected Infrastructure Projects. Keep the detailed implementation and metrics in the Odrava Health experience, and make the corresponding project entry shorter by focusing on architecture and outcome, for example: "Designed a merge-request environment pattern using GitLab CI, Helm, Kubernetes, PostgreSQL seed data, automated end-to-end tests, and automatic cleanup after merge or 48 hours of inactivity." This makes room for the Flaky Test Dashboard project, which is present in the candidate's original material but currently omitted from the CV and provides additional evidence of Python, PostgreSQL, GitLab API, Grafana, and analytical problem-solving.

5. In the Homelab project, clarify the operational and security-related scope using only the existing evidence. Change the second bullet to: "Implemented observability and ingress with Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, and Traefik, and configured cert-manager for TLS certificate management." This wording is concise, ATS-readable, and avoids implying mTLS or production security experience.

6. In the Certifications and Professional Development section, retain the current wording that CKA is preparation only and not certified. Do not change it to "Certified Kubernetes Administrator" or list the certification as obtained, because the candidate's notes explicitly state that the exam has not yet been passed.
